title: Users & Privileges
selectDatabase: Select a database in the connections sidebar to see its users and privileges.
newUserTitle: Create a new user or role
newPolicyTitle: Create a row policy, a quota or a settings profile
connectToSee: Connect "{name}" in the sidebar to see who can reach it.
cannotReadAll: This connection cannot read everything. What is missing:
filter: Find a user, role or policy
noUsers: No users or roles were readable on this connection.
superVia: Unrestricted through the role {role}. The membership is what to take away, not a grant this account does not have.

policies.blurbRow: Which rows of one table an account may see. The first policy on a table hides every row it does not allow, including from accounts it does not name.
policies.blurbQuota: How much an account may use in a window of time: queries, rows read, errors. Going over it fails the query.
policies.blurbProfile: Settings an account runs with, such as a memory ceiling or read-only mode.

restrictiveTitle: Restrictive: ANDed with the other policies, so it can only take rows away
selectToSee: Select a user, role or policy to see what it does.
alsoApplies: What else applies to this account
alsoAppliesNote: These are not privileges. A row policy decides which ROWS of a table are visible, a quota decides how much may be used, and a settings profile decides what the session runs with.
restrictiveTableTitle: ANDed with the other policies on that table
denyTitle: A DENY overrides every grant, including one inherited from a role
grantableTitle: Can pass this privilege on to others

user.one: These are the privileges granted directly. This user also holds a role, which may add more.
user.other: These are the privileges granted directly. This user also holds {count} roles, which may add more.

role.one: These are the privileges granted directly. This role also holds a role, which may add more.
role.other: These are the privileges granted directly. This role also holds {count} roles, which may add more.

login.one: These are the privileges granted directly. This login also holds a role, which may add more.
login.other: These are the privileges granted directly. This login also holds {count} roles, which may add more.

group.one: These are the privileges granted directly. This group also holds a role, which may add more.
group.other: These are the privileges granted directly. This group also holds {count} roles, which may add more.

restrictiveNote: Restrictive: this is ANDed with every other policy on the table, so it can only take rows away.
permissiveNote: Permissive: this is ORed with the other permissive policies on the table. The first policy on a table hides every row no policy allows.
name: Name
conditionHint: A condition on that table's own columns. A row is visible when it is true.
restrictiveHint: Restrictive policies are ANDed with the others, so they can only take rows away. A permissive one is ORed and can give them back.
quotaHint: Counted per account. A window with no limits tracks usage without refusing anything.
settingHint: A setting name as the server spells it, such as max_memory_usage or readonly.
applyNobody: It will exist and apply to nobody until you say who.
mysqlHost: On MySQL the host is part of the account: `app@localhost` and `app@%` are two different accounts with two different sets of privileges.
passwordNote: Typed here and used once, in the statement you are about to review. It is never written to your query history, never sent to a model, and never stored by the app.
mismatch: The two passwords do not match.
letGrant: Let them grant this to others
takesAway: This takes access away. It is not undone by running it again.
showPassword: Show the password in the statement
